training: One pass over ETL training rows per epoch; choose original or corrected proxy per row at random, draw embedded-source synthetic valid controls with replacement. Apply existing trainer augmentation. Supervised all-92 cross-entropy: 0.75 ETL plus 0.25 synthetic; add 0.25 temperature-2 KL to frozen initialization on the same augmented ETL inputs. AdamW, cosine learning rate to 10 percent of initial. No corruption labels are used for training.
selection: Maximize the equal-weight mean known-script top-1 over original and corrected ETL4/5/7 validation inputs; break ties by their mean all-92 cross-entropy, then earliest epoch. No test or KanjiVG input selects checkpoints. Retain every epoch.
promotion: Existing clean/original ETL validation gates remain required: mean corrected ETL4/7 gain >=0.5pp; ETL5/7 losses <=0.5pp; original ETL4 loss <=1pp and original ETL5/7 losses <=0.5pp. Require <=2 fewer canonical identities in known and both scope, >=99 percent positive controls per reference source, no additional >=0.99-confidence non-kana cases, <10MB model, runtime parity and independent seed confirmation. This trial cannot establish modern handwriting or malformed-ink accuracy. No automatic deployment.
negative_policy: Corruption probes have unknown validity and parent labels are provenance only. Evaluate intended-parent recall separately; do not reward accepting corrupted ink as correct. The 26 procedural invalids are a smoke test, not a population false-positive estimate.
scope: Research experiment on existing frozen preparations; source-specific threshold redesign is deferred rather than mixed into this experiment. All ETL derivatives remain private.
confirmation: Frozen after first-trial gates, before confirmation training: same recipe and gates, alternate fine-tuning seed and independently trained residual initialization. Evaluate separately; do not average away a failed seed.
